# Live link checks on a fresh OpenPhish sample

*Eval date 2026-10-22. Generated by `scripts/eval_live_links.py` (measure only: no detection logic was changed). Sample and cached replies: `data/eval_live/`. Re-run: `.venv/bin/python scripts/eval_live_links.py --date 2026-10-22 --offline`.*

## Summary

1. **Phishing, honest setting** (OpenPhish, URLhaus and Tranco switched off): of 96 fresh OpenPhish links (one per registered domain; the feed held only 96 such domains, not 200) the app flagged 73 (76% [67-83]), 35 of them as Likely scam; 10 were rated "No warning signs" and 13 "Can't judge" (free hosting / shorteners). With all signals ON it flags 100%, which is mostly the app finding its own source list.
2. **Benign, honest setting:** 9% [5-16] of 100 Tranco top-10k domains and 20% [13-29] of 100 domains ranked 100k-1M were flagged Suspicious or Likely scam (95% intervals in brackets). The top-10k figure is what you get when Tranco is off; with Tranco on it is 0%, which is circular because the benign domains came from Tranco.
3. **Known gambling miss:** the original spam-ad link was never recorded, so it cannot be replayed. For the 8 gambling sites BUGS.md says the lookup misses (all Tranco top 10k), 8 are rated "No warning signs" with Tranco ON and 7 with it OFF: the miss is still there (section f).

## 1. What was measured

**Function judged:** `shield.core.router.analyse(text, text_model, url_model, live=True)` followed by `shield.core.report.to_report(text, r)`, exactly what `POST /api/analyse` runs (`src/shield/api/main.py`). Text head: `MurilScorer`. Each sampled link is the whole message, so the text head is skipped and the verdict is the link verdict. The verdict is `Report.level`; "flagged" = Likely scam or Suspicious.

**Phishing set (96 links).** OpenPhish public feed, downloaded 2026-10-22T20:53:47+00:00 (SHA-256 `7f1d3bd7ed0cdbcf…`), 300 URLs, 96 unique registered domains (`tldextract.top_domain_under_public_suffix`, which is the same value as the app's `link_domain` for all 96 links). **The target was 200; the feed cannot give more** because 196 of its 300 URLs are pages on free-hosting / user-content platforms (pages.dev alone is one registered domain). All 96 were taken. By kind of host: free_hosting 13, own_domain 83. **Only 83 are ordinary domains** with registry and DNS facts; for the 13 platform-hosted or shortened links the app looks up neither (the registration of pages.dev says nothing about the page), so domain age, certificate age and DNS cannot fire on them by design.

**Benign set (200 domains).** Tranco list on disk (2026-10-22), 100 random domains from ranks 1-10,000 and 100 from 100,000-1,000,000, one `hxxps://<domain>/` each, none also in another set. Skipped before sampling: top 10k: 55 platform / shortener / user content (judged by other rules), 30 already in another set; 100k-1M: 9 already in another set, 3 platform / shortener / user content (judged by other rules). Tranco is not a list of verified-good sites (the 100k-1M band contains some hosting, adult, gambling and a few abusive sites), so a few "false alarms" there can be correct.

**Regression group (22 domains + 3 messages).** Described in section f.

**Not measured / not on:** Google Safe Browsing (no `SAFE_BROWSING_KEY`, so the app skips it), shortener expansion (never run), the sender rule. The URLhaus list is the 30-day export. Samples are only strings: no link was fetched, resolved or connected to (section 8).

**Lifted limits (so the throttle does not fake failures):** the 4 s message deadline of `live.run` is 60 s here; per-call timeout stays 2 s (`net.CALL_TIMEOUT`). RDAP / crt.sh failures were retried twice; the "first attempt only" row below uses the first try of every call, which is what the app does.

RDAP outcomes (ordinary domains only): phishing: date 64, unsupported 18, failed:timeout 1; benign top 10k: date 79, unsupported 20, failed:http_301 1; benign 100k-1M: date 76, unsupported 24. `unsupported` = the TLD has no public RDAP service in IANA's bootstrap file; `no_date` = the registry answered without a registration event; `not_found` = the registry has no such name.

DNS names that no longer resolve (NXDOMAIN): phishing 11 of 83 ordinary domains, benign top 10k 0, benign 100k-1M 0.

Other offline signals that fired (all-ON): homograph R3: phishing 0/96, benign 0/200; brand lookalike R4: phishing 0/96, benign 0/200; raw IP R5: phishing 0/96, benign 0/200; two or more red flags R9: phishing 0/96, benign 0/200. URL model (host-only head) rated Suspicious or higher before the link checks: phishing 68 of 96 at score >= 0.5 (for orientation only; the app's cut-offs are in `models/url_head.joblib`).

## 7. (f) Regression group: gambling / spam-ad links

**The reported link is not available.** BUGS.md says the exact message "was never supplied", so "a spam-ad link that led to a gambling site was rated safe" cannot be replayed. If you have the link or message, add it to `UNLISTED` / `MESSAGES` in the script and rerun. What is tested instead, from what the repo documents: `unlisted` = gambling sites BUGS.md names as missing from the gambling lookup; `unconfirmed` = the 4 gambling-looking domains still `pending_review`; `control` = domains the lookup lists (G1 must say Suspicious); `message` = spam-ad text with a gambling link in the three forms the problem could take. A short link's destination is never fetched, so a spam ad behind a short link can only be "Can't judge" here.

**Result.** Unlisted gambling sites rated "No warning signs": 8 of 8 with all signals ON, 7 of 8 in the honest setting. Unconfirmed: 4 of 4 / 4 of 4. Controls flagged: 10 of 10 (all ON), 10 of 10 (honest). Reading it: P2 ("a well-known website") is on every unlisted top-10k site in the all-ON run, but switching Tranco off still leaves 7 of 8 at "No warning signs", so P2 is not the cause: nothing in the URL model or the link checks knows these sites are gambling sites; only the gambling lookup does. In the message cases the verdict comes from the text head reading the ad wording, not from the link.
